title: Trans-Saharan slave trade
place: Sahara routes from West, Central and East Africa to North Africa and West Asia
summary: For over a thousand years, enslaved people from West, Central and East Africa were marched across the Sahara or shipped via Red Sea ports to North Africa, Egypt, Arabia and the Levant. Estimates range from 10 to 18 million people.
why: A long-running forced migration across the desert, older than the Atlantic trade and lasting into the 20th century.
